title: 60 SQL Practice Queries: PostgreSQL Drills with Answers
summary: Sixty PostgreSQL practice queries over one employees/departments/orders schema, ordered from basic SELECTs to window functions, CTEs and classic interview questions. Each task comes with the solution code and the result it returns on the sample data.

chapters.title: 60 SQL Queries on PostgreSQL
points: 60 practice queries with answers, each one task, one solution, one result
Engine: PostgreSQL 16, every query runs as written
One schema throughout: employees, departments, orders
Eight task families from basics to interview scenarios
Basics, filtering, aggregates and GROUP BY/HAVING
Joins, subqueries, window functions, CTEs and interview classics

chapters.title: The Practice Schema and Sample Rows
points: departments(id, name, location): 5 rows such as Engineering/Austin, Sales/Denver, HR/Austin, Finance/Chicago, Legal/Boston (Legal has no staff)
employees(id, name, dept_id, manager_id, job_title, salary, hire_date): 15 sample rows including one top-level manager with NULL manager_id
orders(id, employee_id, customer, amount, order_date, status): 20 sample rows placed by sales staff
Relationships: employees.dept_id references departments.id, employees.manager_id references employees.id, orders.employee_id references employees.id
Deliberate quirks in the data: tied salaries, one duplicated employee row, an employee with no orders, a NULL manager
Status values in orders: 'paid', 'pending', 'refunded'
How to read each page: task, solution code, result on this data

chapters.title: Basics: Selecting and Shaping Rows
points: Task: List every employee with all columns using SELECT *
Task: Show name and salary, renaming salary to monthly_pay with an alias
Task: List the distinct job titles with SELECT DISTINCT
Task: Show each name with annual pay as salary * 12
Task: Sort employees by salary highest first with ORDER BY ... DESC
Task: Return the 5 highest-paid employees with ORDER BY and LIMIT 5
Task: Skip the first 5 highest-paid and show the next 5 with OFFSET
Task: Show each name in uppercase with its hire year using UPPER and EXTRACT(YEAR FROM hire_date)

chapters.title: Filtering with WHERE
points: Task: Find employees earning more than 70000 with a WHERE comparison
Task: Find employees hired during 2021 using BETWEEN on dates
Task: Find employees in department 1, 2 or 4 with IN
Task: Find names starting with 'A' using LIKE 'A%'
Task: Find names containing 'an' regardless of case using ILIKE
Task: Find employees with no manager using IS NULL (not = NULL)
Task: Find Engineers earning over 90000 or anyone in HR, with parentheses around AND/OR
Task: Label each employee High, Mid or Low pay with CASE WHEN on salary

points: Task: Count all employees with COUNT(*)
Task: Find the average, minimum and maximum salary in one query
Task: Count employees per department with GROUP BY dept_id
Task: Show departments whose average salary exceeds 70000 using HAVING
Task: Total the order amount per employee with SUM and GROUP BY
Task: Count distinct customers with COUNT(DISTINCT customer)
Task: Count orders per status in one row using COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ...)

chapters.title: Joins Across Tables
points: Task: List each employee with their department name using INNER JOIN
Task: Find departments that have no employees using LEFT JOIN ... WHERE e.id IS NULL
Task: Show each employee with their manager's name using a self join
Task: Show each order with the employee who placed it
Task: Find employees who never placed an order with a LEFT JOIN anti-join
Task: Match all employees and departments including unmatched rows on both sides with FULL OUTER JOIN
Task: Generate every department and order-status pair with CROSS JOIN
Task: Total paid sales per department by joining departments, employees and orders

chapters.title: Subqueries
points: Task: Find employees earning more than the company average with a scalar subquery
Task: Find employees earning more than their own department's average with a correlated subquery
Task: Find employees in departments located in Austin using IN (subquery)
Task: Find employees with no orders using NOT EXISTS
Task: Find the highest-paid employee in each department by comparing to a grouped subquery
Task: Show each employee with the department headcount as a scalar subquery in SELECT
Task: Find departments whose average salary beats the overall average using HAVING with a subquery

chapters.title: Window Functions
points: Task: Number employees by salary within each department with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...)
Task: Rank salaries and show how RANK leaves gaps while DENSE_RANK does not
Task: Compute a running total of salary ordered by hire date with SUM() OVER (ORDER BY ...)
Task: Show each order's change from the employee's previous order with LAG
Task: Return the top 2 earners per department by filtering a ROW_NUMBER subquery
Task: Compute a 3-row moving average of order amount using ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
Task: Show each salary as a percent of its department total with SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY ...)

chapters.title: CTEs and Recursive Queries
points: Task: Rewrite the above-average-salary query with a basic WITH clause
Task: Chain two CTEs: department totals, then departments above the mean total
Task: Join a CTE of per-employee sales back to employees to rank the sellers
Task: Walk the org chart down from the top manager with WITH RECURSIVE
Task: Show each employee's management depth level in a recursive CTE
Task: Generate the numbers 1 to 10 with a recursive CTE
Task: Delete rows and return them in one step with a data-modifying CTE and RETURNING

chapters.title: Real Interview Scenarios
points: Task: Find the 3rd highest distinct salary using DENSE_RANK
Task: Find the second highest salary with ORDER BY ... OFFSET 1 and no ties handling
Task: Find duplicate employee rows with GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

Task: Find employees who earn more than their manager with a self join
Task: Build cumulative monthly revenue with date_trunc and a running SUM window

chapters.title: SQL Drills Cheatsheet
points: Clause order as written: SELECT, FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT
Logical execution order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT
WHERE filters rows, HAVING filters groups
NULL rules: IS NULL, COALESCE, NOT IN breaks on NULLs so prefer NOT EXISTS
Join picker: INNER keeps matches, LEFT keeps all left rows, anti-join finds missing matches
ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK on tied values
Pattern: top N per group is a ROW_NUMBER window plus a filter in an outer query
Pattern: nth highest, duplicates, running totals each have one standard solution
